Frankie Ervin (lead vocals, toured as The Shields)

podcast.title: Accidental Million-Selling Group
podcast.body: The Shields originated as a scratch vocal group assembled by Jesse Belvin for Frankie Ervin's recording of "You Cheated." The song unexpectedly became a massive hit, credited to The Shields by Dot Records, effectively creating another million-selling group that Belvin was inadvertently involved with. "But while Belvin had accidentally put together yet another million-selling group, he had also moved on to bigger things."

podcast.title: Changing Lineups and Belvin's Departure
podcast.body: For The Shields' third record, only Jesse Belvin remained from the original recording lineup, indicating the transient nature of the group. Subsequent recordings by The Shields did not feature Belvin at all, as he had moved on to bigger career opportunities with RCA, signaling the end of his direct involvement. "So The Third Shields record only featured Belvin out of The Original lineup, and subsequent recordings didn't even feature him."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Label's Avoidance of Solo Artist Demands
podcast.body: The recording of "You Cheated" was an independent production leased to Dot Records. The label deliberately credited the song to a generic group name, The Shields, rather than Frankie Ervin as a solo artist. This decision was reportedly made to avoid promoting a solo singer who might later demand credits, royalties, or more money, especially given that Ervin was Black. "Somewhere along the line someone decided that it was better to have a generic group name, rather than promote it as by a solo singer, who might get ideas about wanting money."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 47: "Goodnight My Love" by Jesse Belvin

podcast.title: Outselling the Original by a Black Group
podcast.body: In an unusual turn for the music industry at the time, The Shields' sound-alike version of "You Cheated," performed by a black group, managed to outsell the original recording by the white group, The Slades. This was a notable reversal of the typical industry trend, where covers by black artists rarely surpassed white originals commercially. "This time, a sound-like record by a black group managed to outsell the original by a white group."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 47: "Goodnight My Love" by Jesse Belvin

podcast.title: Touring Lineup vs. Recording Lineup
podcast.body: Due to original recording members (Jesse Belvin, Johnny "Guitar" Watson, Tommy "Buster" Williams, Mel Williams) being under contract to other labels, Frankie Ervin toured and made TV appearances as "The Shields" backed by random singers assembled by the record label. Only for the follow-up, "Nature Boy," did some original members reunite, highlighting the ad-hoc nature of the group's performance lineup. "Irving started touring and making TV appearances as The Shields, backed by some random singers the record label had pulled together."
